correctness.rationale: Conditional on the reflected path, every excursion sign is symmetric, so each nonzero time contributes conditional positive-occupation probability one half. This proves the exact conditional mean. The local-time mean and variance follow from exact return probabilities, a telescoping central-binomial identity, the Markov property, and the coefficient convolution of (1-z)^(-1/2). Exhaustive path enumeration independently verifies both the reflected-path and local-time conditional regressions through eight half-horizons.

value.rationale: Local time and one-sided occupation are canonical random-walk path functionals that are usually studied through arcsine laws, path transforms, and scaling limits. The theorem gives a finite-horizon structural regression rather than another marginal formula: once the complete reflected path is fixed, zero visits remove exactly one half-unit of expected positive occupation each. Combining this with the exact local-time variance yields a closed finite covariance and identifies precisely which part of occupation is second-moment orthogonal to local time.
